review.note: Retracted in M22: the orthographic agreement signed in Lisbon on 16 December 1990 by the seven lusophone states, after ten years of negotiation between the academies of Lisbon and Rio. This one is genuinely Portuguese history and is retracted only because the atlas holds nothing of the field it belongs to: no CPLP, no language policy, no record of the agreement’s long and contested entry into force. Among the best candidates in M22 for being written back in.

title: Portuguese Language Orthographic Agreement of 1990
summary: Wikidata item Q1113432, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "international treaty to create a unified orthography for Portuguese". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
